objectives: Sort things into living, once living and non-living.
Give examples from home and school.
reviewNotes: Characteristics are simplified (no MRS GREN terms).
Syllabus references, scope and level of difficulty are to be checked against the official text; all facts, formulas and worked examples to be verified by a teacher before release.

blocks.title: Signs of life
blocks.md: A **living thing** does these things: it **feeds** (takes in food), **breathes**, **grows**, **moves** (animals move around, plants move slowly towards light), **reproduces** (makes young ones or seeds), **gets rid of waste** and **senses** what is around it. A goat, a maize plant and a child are living.

blocks.caption: Examples of living and non-living things.
blocks.alt: A table with two columns: living (goat, maize plant, child, mushroom) and non-living (stone, water, chair, plastic bottle).

blocks.title: Non-living and once-living
blocks.md: **Non-living** things never lived: stone, water, plastic, metal, air. Some things were **once living**: a dry leaf, a wooden stool (from a tree), leather shoes (from an animal). They no longer feed, breathe or grow.

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.md:
- Saying that a plant is not living because it does not walk.
- Thinking that fire or the sun is living because it moves or gives light.
- Putting a wooden table in the living group: it is made from a tree that was once living.

blocks.title: Example 1
blocks.statement: Is a mango tree living? Give two reasons.
steps: A mango tree grows from a seed and gets taller each year.
It also takes in water and makes fruit with seeds (it reproduces).
blocks.answer: Yes: it grows and it makes seeds.

blocks.title: Example 2
blocks.statement: Sort: a hen, a stone, a dry leaf, a goat.
steps: Hen and goat feed, breathe, grow and move: living.
Stone never lived: non-living. A dry leaf came from a plant: once living.
blocks.answer: living: hen, goat; non-living: stone; once living: dry leaf.
